recap.title: The American Express
recap.body: Opened his 2026 season with a victory at The American Express for his 20th PGA TOUR title. Became the first player to reach 20 PGA TOUR wins since Rory McIlroy (2021 CJ CUP in South Carolina), and the first player since Tiger Woods (2000 U.S. Open at 24 years, 5 months, 19 days of age) to earn 20 PGA TOUR wins prior to turning 30 years old. Earned his 20th TOUR title in what was his 151st career start, only trailing Tiger Woods (95 starts) for the fewest career starts to reach 20 TOUR victories since 1970. Entered the final round one stroke behind 54-hole leader Si Woo Kim, but closed in 6-under 66 (with a double bogey on the par-3 17th) for a four-stroke victory over a quartet of co-runners-up (Jason Day, Ryan Gerard, Matt McCarty, Andrew Putnam). Marked Scheffler's first win in a PGA TOUR season debut, as well as his seventh win in his last 13 starts on TOUR.

recap.title: FedEx St. Jude Championship
recap.body: Earned his 21st PGA TOUR title and second win of the 2026 season with an eight-stroke victory at TPC Southwind, marking the largest margin of victory by any player on TOUR since his eight-stroke win at the 2025 CJ CUP Byron Nelson. Became the fifth player in the last 40 years with multiple wins of eight-plus strokes on TOUR, following Tiger Woods (10), Ernie Els (two), Dustin Johnson (two), and Rory McIlroy (two). At 30 years, 1 month, 26 days of age, became the third-youngest player to reach 21 career wins on TOUR since 1970, only behind Jack Nicklaus (27 years, 1 day at 1967 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am) and Tiger Woods (24 years, 6 months, 23 days at 2000 Open Championship). Converted a two-stroke 54-hole lead into an eight-stroke victory, improving to 12-of-15 converting to victory as the solo 54-hole leader.

recap.title: Valspar Championship
recap.body: Made a 13-foot, 11-inch birdie putt on the 72nd hole of regulation, the par-4 18th on the Copperhead Course at Innisbrook Resort, for a one-stroke victory over David Lipsky and his third PGA TOUR title. Prior to the final round, had not birdied No. 18 in 11 previous rounds at the event. Totaled 11-under 273 with four rounds in the 60s and went bogey-free across his final 36 holes, becoming the third winner of the event to record a bogey-free final round (Luke Donald/2012, Kevin Streelman/2013). Following the win, rose to No. 6 in the Official World Golf Ranking, the highest ranking of his career and his first appearance in the top 10 since April 2024.

recap.title: RBC Heritage
recap.body: Earned his fourth PGA TOUR title as he defeated Scottie Scheffler with a birdie on the first playoff hole, the par-4 18th at Harbour Town Golf Links, hitting a 4-iron to 13 feet, 4 inches to set up the winning putt. Marked his second TOUR win in a three-start span (Valspar Championship) and secured his first multi-win season on TOUR. Previously won the 2023 RBC Heritage, making him the 11th player to win the event multiple times. In the final round, birdied two of the first three holes (par-4 first and third), but bogeyed the 72nd hole of regulation as he closed in 1-under 70. Held a one-stroke lead through 36 holes at 14-under 128, the second-lowest 36-hole score in tournament history (126/Stewart Cink/2021), and a three-stroke lead through 54 holes at 17-under 196, the second-lowest 54-hole score in tournament history (195/Stewart Cink/2021). Improved to 3-for-5 converting the 54-hole lead/co-lead into victory, having previously accomplished the feat in wins at the 2022 U.S. Open and 2023 RBC Heritage. Following the win, rose to No. 3 in the Official World Golf Ranking, his first appearance in the top five.

recap.title: Zurich Classic of New Orleans
recap.body: With his younger brother, Alex Fitzpatrick, as his partner, earned his fifth PGA TOUR title at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans. Won for a second consecutive week (RBC Heritage) and for the third time in his last four starts on TOUR (Valspar Championship). Became the first player since 2024 to win back-to-back TOUR events (Scottie Scheffler/2024 Masters Tournament and 2024 RBC Heritage). Totaled a tournament-record 31-under 257 at TPC Louisiana off the strength of a 15-under 57 in the third round, the lowest 18-hole score in the Four-ball format since the tournament became a team event in 2017. Marked the fourth consecutive year Matt and Alex played the event together (T19/2023, T11/2024, MC/2025).

events.name: the Memorial Tournament presented by Workday

recap.title: THE CJ CUP Byron Nelson
recap.body: Wyndham Clark wins THE CJ CUP Byron Nelson, his fourth PGA TOUR title in his 201st start at 32 years, 5 months, 15 days. With a final-round 60, one of four players to post 60 or better in the final round en route to victory on record (David Duval/1999 American Express/59, Stuart Appleby/2010 Greenbrier Classic/59, Tommy Gainey/2012 RSM Classic/60) and marks the second time in his career (2024 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am/60*). Win came in his fourth start at THE CJ CUP Byron Nelson (MC/2019, T39/2021, MC/2022, Won/2026) and marked his first top-10 of his season. Led the field in Strokes Gained: Putting (12.573).

recap.title: U.S. Open
recap.body: Earned his fifth PGA TOUR title and second major championship (previously won the 2023 U.S. Open) with a one-stroke victory over Sam Burns. Led by two strokes through 18 holes, four strokes through 36 holes, and six strokes through 54 holes as he became the ninth wire-to-wire winner in U.S. Open history, following Walter Hagen (1914), Jim Barnes (1921), Ben Hogan (1953), Tony Jacklin (1970), Tiger Woods (2000, 2002), Rory McIlroy (2011), and Martin Kaymer (2014). Marked the first wire-to-wire victory in a major championship since Brooks Koepka at the 2019 PGA Championship. At 4-under 276, tied Retief Goosen (2004) for the lowest 72-hole score relative to par in the five U.S. Opens contested at Shinnecock Hills Golf Club since 1896. Following the win, rose to No. 8 in the Official World Golf Ranking, marking his first appearance in the top 10 since March 2025.

recap.title: BMW Championship
recap.body: Earned his third win of the 2026 season and sixth career PGA TOUR title at the BMW Championship, converting a five-stroke 54-hole lead into a three-stroke victory at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis, Missouri. Closed the final round with three consecutive birdies as he improved to 4-for-5 converting the 54-hole lead/co-lead into victory.

recap.title: THE PLAYERS Championship
recap.body: Earned his second PGA TOUR title at THE PLAYERS Championship with a one-stroke victory over Matt Fitzpatrick, marking his second win in 11 starts after he went winless (with seven runner-up finishes) in his first 93 TOUR starts. Trailed 54-hole leader Ludvig Aberg by four strokes and closed with a 4-under 68 in the final round, highlighted by a bogey-free 3-under 33 on the back nine with birdies at the par-4 10th, par-3 13th, and par-3 17th. Parred the 72nd hole of regulation, the par-4 18th, after a 375-yard drive, the longest by any player on the hole in the ShotLink era (since 2003). Birdied No. 17 each of the final three rounds, becoming the first winner of THE PLAYERS Championship to accomplish the feat. Led the field in proximity on approach shots (28 feet, 1 inch) and scrambling (16 of 21). With the victory, rose to No. 4 in the Official World Golf Ranking, marking his first appearance in the top 10.

recap.title: Cadillac Championship
recap.body: Recorded a wire-to-wire victory, converting a one-stroke 18-hole lead, five-stroke 36-hole lead and six-stroke 54-hole lead into a six-stroke win for his third PGA TOUR title. Marked his second PGA TOUR win by six strokes (2025 Wyndham Championship). Totaled 19-under 269 at Trump National Doral’s Blue Monster Course. In the final round, called a penalty on himself (breach of Rule 9.4, a player caused their ball at rest to move) on the par-4 second and saved par with a 13-foot, 6-inch putt. Followed Justin Rose as the second wire-to-wire winner of the 2026 PGA TOUR Season.

recap.title: Sony Open in Hawaii
recap.body: Earned his third PGA TOUR win in what was his 69th career start, securing a two-stroke victory at 16-under 264 with a bogey-free 3-under 32 on the back nine of the final round. Marked his second victory in his last eight starts on TOUR (2025 Genesis Scottish Open). Became the first player since Tom Kim (2023 Shriners Children's Open / 44th start) to earn his first three PGA TOUR wins in less than 70 starts. Led the field in Strokes Gained: Off the Tee (4.352) and went 6-for-6 on sand saves. Rose to No. 17 in the Official World Golf Ranking following the victory, his first time being ranked among the top 20 players in the world.

recap.title: WM Phoenix Open
recap.body: Holed a 27-foot birdie putt on the first playoff hole (par-4 18th at TPC Scottsdale), defeating Hideki Matsuyama for his fourth PGA TOUR title at the WM Phoenix Open. Opened the tournament with a bogey-free 8-under 63 for a two-stroke lead through 18 holes, but began the final round four strokes behind Matsuyama, the outright 54-hole leader. Closed in 7-under 64, bouncing back from a bogey at the par-3 12th with birdies on five of the final six holes of regulation (Nos. 13, 14, 15, 17, 18). Marked his third victory in his last 10 starts on TOUR (2025 Genesis Scottish Open, 2026 Sony Open in Hawaii), which propelled him to No. 5 in the Official World Golf Ranking. Prior to his win at the 2025 Genesis Scottish Open, stood No. 158 in the OWGR.

recap.title: John Deere Classic
recap.body: Earned his fifth PGA TOUR title – and fourth TOUR win in a span of 357 days – with a one-stroke victory over Max Homa in his 85th career start on TOUR. Began the final round five strokes behind 54-hole co-leaders Lucas Glover and Lee Hodges, and closed with a bogey-free 9-under 62 for his first win in four appearances at the John Deere Classic. Became the fifth player since 2000 to earn five PGA TOUR titles in 85 starts or less, following Collin Morikawa (51 starts), Rory McIlroy (52 starts), Bryson DeChambeau (73 starts) and Jordan Spieth (76 starts).

events.name: Arnold Palmer Invitational presented by Mastercard

recap.title: AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am
recap.body: Earned his seventh PGA TOUR title at the 2026 A&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am, two-putting for birdie from the greenside rough of the par-5 18th at Pebble Beach Golf Links for a one-stroke victory over Min Woo Lee and Sepp Straka. Played the last four holes of the final round in 2-under par with three birdies (Nos. 15, 16, 18) and a bogey at the par-3 17th. Totaled 22-under 266 for the tournament, tying Brandt Snedeker (2015) for the lowest winning score relative to par in tournament history. Ended a winless drought of 2 years, 3 months, 24 days (and 46 PGA TOUR starts), as his previous TOUR victory came in October 2023 at the Baycurrent Classic. Marked his third TOUR victory in his home state of California (previous: 2019 Barracuda Championship, 2020 PGA Championship at TPC Harding Park). Carded a 10-under 62 in the third round as he hit all 18 greens in regulation, becoming the seventh player since 1985 to accomplish the feat at Pebble Beach Golf Links during the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am.

recap.title: Masters Tournament
recap.body: Earned his 30th PGA TOUR title (tying Horton Smith for 16th all time) and sixth major championship (tying Nick Faldo, Lee Trevino, and Phil Mickelson for 12th all time) as he successfully defended his title at the 2026 Masters Tournament. Converted the largest 36-hole lead in Masters Tournament history (six strokes) into a one-stroke victory over world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, marking the third major championship since 1986 in which the two top finishers (in either order) were the No. 1 and No. 2 players in the Official World Golf Ranking (2002 U.S. Open/Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson; 1991 Masters Tournament/Ian Woosnam and Jose Maria Olazabal). Followed Jack Nicklaus (1965, 1966), Nick Faldo (1989, 1990), and Tiger Woods (2001, 2002) as the fourth player in history to successfully defend their title at the Masters Tournament. Shared the 54-hole lead with Cameron Young and improved to 6-for-8 converting 54-hole leads/co-leads into victory in major championships. Closed in 1-under 71, overcoming a double bogey at the par-3 fourth and notably making back-to-back birdies at the par-3 12th and par-5 13th. In the second round, built a six-stroke lead after a 7-under 65 which featured nine birdies, his most in a single round at a major championship (previous: eight/2014 PGA Championship/R1).

recap.title: The Genesis Invitational
recap.body: Earned his first PGA TOUR title at the 2026 Genesis Invitational, totaling 18-under 266 for a one-stroke victory over Kurt Kitayama and Rory McIlroy, his playing partner in the final group of the final round. In his tournament debut and 66th career start on TOUR, built a six-stroke lead through 54 holes after an opening-round 5-under 66 and consecutive rounds of 7-under 64, tying the 54-hole tournament scoring record of 194 previously established by Joaquin Niemann (2022). Six-stroke lead through 54 holes was one stroke shy of the tournament record for largest 54-hole lead (Arnold Palmer/1966). Became the first player since Pat Fitzsimons in 1975 to win The Genesis Invitational in their tournament debut. Also became the 13th player and first since 2015 (James Hahn) to make The Genesis Invitational their first PGA TOUR title.

recap.title: Charles Schwab Challenge
recap.body: Defeated Eric Cole in a playoff to win the Charles Schwab Challenge, his sixth PGA TOUR title in his 321st start at the age of 37 years, 1 month, 19 days. With a birdie-3 on the first playoff hole (No. 18), improves to 2-1 in playoffs. Entered the final round three shots back from the lead, birdied his final three holes to tie the lead and force a playoff and become the second winner of the Charles Schwab Challenge to make birdie or better on the final three holes (first: Jordan Spieth/2016).

recap.title: Arnold Palmer Invitational presented by Mastercard
recap.body: Earned his third PGA TOUR title as he defeated Daniel Berger on the first playoff hole, the par-4 18th at Arnold Palmer's Bay Hill Club and Lodge. Trailed Berger by five strokes with nine holes remaining in the final round, but made four consecutive birdies on Nos. 10-13 and eagled the par-5 16th as he carded a 5-under 31 on the back nine, the lowest final-round back nine by a winner of the event since 2018 (Rory McIlroy/31), and forced the first playoff at the Arnold Palmer Invitational presented by Mastercard since 1999. Improved to 3-0 in playoffs on TOUR, having previously defeated Denny McCarthy to win the 2024 Valero Texas Open and Patrick Rodgers to win the 2023 Barracuda Championship. Led the field in Strokes Gained: Putting (10.605) and Strokes Gained: Around the Green (5.664), which marked the second-best combined Strokes Gained: Around the Green and Putting performance of the ShotLink era (since 2003), only behind Aaron Baddeley at the 2004 Chrysler Classic of Tucson. Became the fourth PGA TOUR winner in the ShotLink era who led the field in both Strokes Gained: Around the Green and Strokes Gained: Putting, following Geoff Ogilvy (2009 Sentry), Tiger Woods (2009 Arnold Palmer Invitational presented by Mastercard), and Jordan Spieth (2016 Sentry). Notably finished with -3.637 Strokes Gained: Off the Tee, the second-worst performance in the category by a winner in the ShotLink era (Cameron Smith/2022 PLAYERS Championship).

recap.title: Texas Children's Houston Open
recap.body: Converted a three-stroke 36-hole lead and one-stroke 54-hole lead into a five-stroke victory at Memorial Park Golf Course, earning his fifth PGA TOUR title and first since the 2019 U.S. Open (a span of six years, nine months, and 13 days). Totaled 21-under 259 as he broke the Texas Children’s Houston Open 72-hole scoring record previously established by Min Woo Lee (260 in 2025). The year prior, finished T2 at the 2025 Texas Children’s Houston Open, making him the first player to finish runner-up and win the same tournament the next season since Robert MacIntyre (2023, 2024 Genesis Scottish Open). Marked his third start since he publicly revealed at the 2026 PLAYERS Championship he was diagnosed with PTSD in the wake of brain surgery, which he underwent in September 2023.

recap.title: Truist Championship
recap.body: Earned his first PGA TOUR title with a two-stroke victory over Rickie Fowler and Nicolai Højgaard, totaling 15-under 269 at Quail Hollow Club, highlighted by a bogey-free 7-under 64 in the third round. Followed Viktor Hovland as the second Norwegian to win on the PGA TOUR. Became the seventh player to earn their first PGA TOUR title at the Truist Championship, following Anthony Kim (2008), Rory McIlroy (2010), Rickie Fowler (2012), Derek Ernst (2013), Max Homa (2019), and Wyndham Clark (2023). In the two weeks prior to the Truist Championship, finished T2 at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans and T14 at the Cadillac Championship (as the last player who gained entry to the 72-player field), earning enough FedExCup points to qualify for the Truist Championship via fifth and final position in the Aon Swing 5.

recap.title: Valero Texas Open
recap.body: Earned his third PGA TOUR title at the 2026 Valero Texas Open with a one-stroke victory over co-runners-up Michael Kim, Robert MacIntyre and Matt Wallace. Closed in 5-under 67, highlighted by a birdie at the par-3 16th and eagle at the par-4 17th, with the latter playing 306 yards for the final round; he made a 9-foot, 7-inch eagle putt on No. 17. Previously earned his first TOUR win at the 2022 Valero Texas Open, making him the 11th multi-time winner of the event. Following the win, rose to No. 5 in the Official World Golf Ranking, marking his first appearance in the top five.

recap.title: Zurich Classic of New Orleans
recap.body: With his older brother, Matt Fitzpatrick, as his partner, earned his first PGA TOUR title at the Zurich Classic of New Orleans in what was his 11th career start on TOUR. With the victory, earned PGA TOUR membership for the first time, as well as exemptions into the 2026 PGA Championship, the four remaining Signature Events in 2026 (Cadillac Championship, Truist Championship, the Memorial Tournament presented by Workday, Travelers Championship), and the 2027 PLAYERS Championship. Marked the first TOUR win by a non-member and sponsor exemption since Michael Brennan (2025 Bank of Utah Championship). Totaled a tournament-record 31-under 257 at TPC Louisiana off the strength of a 15-under 57 in the third round, the lowest 18-hole score in the Four-ball format since the tournament became a team event in 2017. Marked the fourth consecutive year Alex and Matt played the event together (T19/2023, T11/2024, MC/2025).

recap.title: Travelers Championship
recap.body: Earned his eighth PGA TOUR title as he defeated Scottie Scheffler with a birdie on the first playoff hole (contested Monday morning), the par-4 18th at TPC River Highlands. Totaled a career-low 21-under 259 as he closed with a final-round 1-under 69, highlighted by three consecutive birdies on Nos. 13-15. Improved to 5-for-6 converting 54-hole leads/co-leads into victory, as he led by one stroke through 54 holes. Had not finished better than T11 in five previous starts at the Travelers Championship.

recap.title: Genesis Scottish Open
recap.body: At 24 years and 21 days of age, earned his fourth PGA TOUR title and ended a winless drought of two years, eight months, and 27 days with a two-stroke victory over Min Woo Lee. Tied Hideki Matsuyama with the third-most PGA TOUR wins on record by an international player prior to turning 25 years of age, only trailing Rory McIlroy (six) and Sergio Garcia (five). Also tied Si Woo Kim for the second-most PGA TOUR wins by a player from South Korea, with both trailing eight-time TOUR winner K.J. Choi. Carded a bogey-free 6-under 64 in the final round and totaled 17-under 263 at The Renaissance Club; he was the only player with a bogey-free final round. Co-led (with Jordan Smith) through 36 holes, improving to 2-for-3 converting 36-hole leads/co-leads into victory on TOUR (2022 Wyndham Championship/Won; 2024 Travelers Championship/P2).

recap.title: the Memorial Tournament presented by Workday
recap.body: Earned his fourth PGA TOUR title (and first since the 2024 Shriners Children’s Open) as he defeated Ryan Gerard with a par on the second playoff hole, the par-4 18th at Muirfield Village Golf Club. After play was suspended Saturday afternoon, completed the majority of his third round Sunday morning and carried a four-stroke lead into the final round. Played the first 13 holes of the final round at 3-over par, but rallied and forced a playoff with birdies on the par-4 14th, par-5 15th, and par-4 18th. Followed David Edwards (1992) and Hideki Matsuyama (2014) as the third player who forced a playoff with a birdie on the 18th hole at the Memorial Tournament (all three won). Improved to 3-for-5 converting the 54-hole lead/co-lead into victory, having previously accomplished the feat in wins at the 2022 John Deere Classic and 2024 Shriners Children’s Open. Entered the tournament at No. 94 in the Official World Golf Ranking, making him the lowest-ranked player in the OWGR to win the Memorial Tournament since William McGirt, who stood No. 102 in 2016.

recap.title: RBC Canadian Open
recap.body: In his 239th career start, earned his first PGA TOUR title with a two-stroke victory over Matt Fitzpatrick. Off the strength of a 7-under 63 in the second round, totaled 17-under 263 at TPC Toronto at Osprey Valley (North Course). Made four birdies on the back nine of his final round, including a chip-in birdie at the par-4 12th. Became the first American to win the RBC Canadian Open since Dustin Johnson in 2018 and the first American to earn their first PGA TOUR title at the event since Chez Reavie in 2008. Following the win, rose to No. 40 in the Official World Golf Ranking, marking his first appearance in the top 50.

recap.title: PGA Championship
recap.body: Captured his first major title at the 2026 PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf Club in his 13th career start in a major. Became the first Englishman to win the PGA Championship since 1919. Carded scores of 70-69-67-65 for a 72-hole score of 9-under 271, securing a three-stroke margin of victory over Jon Rahm and Alex Smalley. Became the eighth major championship winner in history to lower his score in each round and the first since 1998 (Mark O’Meara/Masters Tournament). Marked his second victory on TOUR after winning the 2024 Wyndham Championship.

recap.title: Rocket Classic
recap.body: Earned his first PGA TOUR title with a bogey-free 7-under 63 in the final round, overcoming a four-stroke deficit with five back-nine birdies to secure a two-stroke victory over Xander Schauffele. Marked the largest come-from-behind win in tournament history (previous: three strokes/Bryson DeChambeau/2020). Birdied the 72nd hole of regulation as he totaled 18-under 262 at Detroit Golf Club, tying the 72-hole tournament scoring record (Tony Finau/2022). Followed Ludvig Aberg as the second player who finished No. 1 in the PGA TOUR University Ranking to win on the PGA TOUR.

recap.title: Cognizant Classic in The Palm Beaches
recap.body: Earned his third PGA TOUR title in his 94th career start on TOUR, closing out a two-stroke victory over Shane Lowry, Taylor Moore, and Austin Smotherman with consecutive bogey-free rounds of 5-under 66 on the weekend. Trailed Lowry by three strokes with three holes remaining in regulation, but birdied the par-3 17th as Lowry made back-to-back double bogeys at Nos. 16 and 17, ultimately creating Echavarria's two-stroke margin of victory at 17-under 267. Made the fewest number of bogeys of any player in the field (three), all of which came in the second round. Followed Camilo Villegas (2010) as the second Colombian to win the event.

recap.title: Wyndham Championship
recap.body: Earned his second PGA TOUR title with a three-stroke victory at Sedgefield Country Club, where he played the weekend in 13-under 127 (63-64) and made five consecutive birdies on the front nine (Nos. 4-8) of his final round. Shared the 54-hole lead with Beau Hossler, improving to 2-for-2 converting the 54-hole lead/co-lead into victory (2025 Bank of Utah Championship). Entered the week at No. 105 in the FedExCup standings, moving into the top 50 and qualifying for the FedExCup Playoffs with the victory.

recap.title: 3M Open
recap.body: Earned his first PGA TOUR title in his 13th career start (and third start on TOUR since turning professional and accepting membership via PGA TOUR University Accelerated), carding back-to-back bogey-free rounds of 10-under 61 and 5-under 66 on the weekend at the 3M Open for a three-stroke victory over world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler. Converted a three-stroke 54-hole lead into victory, totaling 25-under 259 to break the 72-hole tournament scoring record at TPC Twin Cities (previous record: 260/Lee Hodges/2023). At 21 years, two months, three days of age, became the eighth-youngest PGA TOUR winner since 2017, and became the youngest American to win a TOUR event by multiple strokes since Ralph Guldahl (20 years, two months, 10 days) at the 1932 WM Phoenix Open. Victory came just 35 days after the final round of the 2026 U.S. Open (June 21), his last round as an amateur. Became the first player to earn a PGA TOUR win after accepting membership through PGA TOUR University Accelerated.

recap.title: Puerto Rico Open
recap.body: Earned his first PGA TOUR title in his 35th career start on TOUR, converting a one-stroke 54-hole lead into a one-stroke victory over Chandler Blanchet at 17-under 271. Closed with a bogey-free 5-under 67, as he eagled the par-5 sixth and birdied the par-3 seventh, par-4 13th, and par-5 14th at Grand Reserve Golf Club. Played the final two rounds without a bogey, made the fewest scores of bogey or worse of any player in the field (two), and led the field in Scrambling (19 of 21).
